result.summary: The page is largely well-composed, but the fixed bottom tab bar is clearly broken: the iOS home-indicator bar is drawn straight through the tab icons and the icons themselves sit flush against (and are clipped by) the bottom screen edge, indicating missing safe-area padding. A couple of smaller cosmetic inconsistencies were also found (unlabeled tab items and inconsistent favorite-button treatment).

issues.description: The bottom navigation bar does not respect the device safe area: the black home-indicator pill overlaps and visually cuts through the Search and Orders tab icons, and the icons are positioned at the very bottom edge of the screen with no bottom padding, making them look clipped and hard to tap.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom safe-area inset padding (e.g. env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) plus ~8-12px of internal padding to the tab bar, and increase its height so icons sit fully above the home indicator with a comfortable 44px+ tap target.

issues.description: The four bottom tab items show icons only, with no text labels (Home, Search, Orders, Account), which makes the middle icons (magnifier vs. receipt) ambiguous and reduces clarity of the active state.
issues.suggestion: Add short text labels under each tab icon (or at minimum accessible labels/tooltips) and give the active tab a consistent highlight treatment.

issues.description: Favorite (heart) buttons are styled inconsistently between cards: the ramen card's heart sits directly on the image with no backing shape, while the pizza card's heart has a dark translucent circular background. On lighter imagery the bare white heart would have poor contrast.
issues.suggestion: Apply the same semi-transparent circular scrim behind the heart icon on every card so the control is consistently visible and legible over any image.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' row, the first thumbnail uses a light gray studio background while the following thumbnails use dark, moody backgrounds, creating a visually uneven carousel.
issues.suggestion: Normalize thumbnail treatment (consistent background/crop or a subtle uniform overlay) so the row reads as a cohesive set.
